item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukraine has deployed naval drones to strike Russian warships in Libya's Benghazi port, claiming lawful self-defence, while Russia has violated Finnish airspace with a helicopter and Polish airspace with an unmanned aerial vehicle. NATO's chief has pledged defence against a Russian space threat after reports of a planned nuclear satellite, and MI5 has warned UK firms supplying Ukraine of sabotage risk. The UN Security Council warned that winter attacks on Ukraine's power grid and Black Sea shipping threaten lives and global food supplies. Battle-related deaths totaled 75,767 in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli air strikes have continued to target senior Hamas security officials in Gaza, killing at least two named figures, while Israel has redirected $90 million from border community recovery budgets to defense and detained a Polish lawmaker ahead of a West Bank visit. Gaza health officials have warned of a rising meningitis epidemic and a night of arson has been linked to Israeli Jewish terrorism, and Israel's top court described West Bank settlers as acting like militias. Israeli minister Ben-Gvir has been accused of seeking a religious war over mosque raids, and Israel has pledged to advance delayed sewage repairs in Gaza under international pressure. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

US sanctions on Hezbollah affiliates are viewed as having limited impact, and Iran is reported to be developing chemical weapons. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted Houthi drones and missiles over the Red Sea and in western Yemen, and hit a Houthi arms depot east of Taiz. Saudi civil defence reported that 11 people were injured in the tower drone strike. New Delhi condemned the attack on the tower. 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
US officials are discussing a military training and demining mission for Syrian forces while a budget shortfall threatens the chemical weapons watchdog’s work in Syria. Israeli forces raided southern Syria, wounding Syrian soldiers, and a drone strike in western Sweida injured four Syrian internal security personnel. Two Christian young men were found dead in the Damascus countryside and suspects, including a church guard, were arrested after a robbery at a Homs church. A son of a Daesh leader was killed in Homs and a mortar attack killed one civilian and injured three others in Syria. 2,732 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
The Iraqi prime minister ordered the ministry to take direct control of oilfields held by Kurdish parties, prompting the KDP and PUK to unite in opposition and warn Baghdad against unilateral decisions. Security forces dismissed the border crossings chief and a border official, installed new commanders in Kirkuk, and seized trucks in a fuel-smuggling operation. Iraqi security also seized two drone launchers in Maysan and reported a drone hit an Azadi camp minutes after a missile strike. The conflict recorded 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Sudan's civil war: the situation
item.description:
Drone strikes have hit a United Nations building and residential areas in Khartoum, killing four people and threatening humanitarian operations, while RSF forces assaulted aid offices in Nyala and a shelter in West Kordofan, causing civilian casualties. New defections include the RSF counterintelligence chief, a commander and a group joining the Sudanese army in Khartoum, indicating shifting loyalties within the conflict. Ethiopia has offered to host inclusive Sudan peace talks and proposes a national unity government, but Sudan rejected the offer and questioned Ethiopia's neutrality. The war produced 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Ethiopia has intensified its regional role by offering to host a comprehensive Sudanese dialogue and Abiy Ahmed is urging Sudanese parties to join a mediation table, while drone strikes linked to Ethiopia killed four people and damaged a United Nations building in Khartoum. At the same time, artillery shelling by Ethiopian forces in Alamata killed 14 civilians, prompting Amnesty International to call for a war crimes investigation in Tigray. Leaked intelligence suggests coordination between Eritrean and Sudanese actors in drone strikes on Mekelle and Assosa. Ethiopian forces have regained control of border areas near Badme, and clashes continue along the Afar-Somali border over territory, drought and resources. 2,824 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Federal forces have relaunched the previously failed Banooda operation, moving a major troop convoy while the defence minister reported killing 285 al-Shabaab fighters, including several commanders, in Bay, Shabelle and Hiiraan. The United States conducted airstrikes on three al-Shabaab sites in Somalia, and Uganda’s president met Somalia’s president to strengthen security cooperation, with the Ugandan army chief visiting Somali troops amid a withdrawal from Barawe. Climate shocks and insecurity are driving displacement, with over 18,000 people displaced by fighting in Southwest State as flood threats loom, and the UN warns that unrest in Ethiopia could weaken African Union security operations. The conflict produced 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Jihadist militants have intensified attacks in Niger state, killing dozens of civilians, 11 soldiers in the southeast, at least 16 soldiers near the Malian border, and 25 soldiers in another strike, while Fulani communities suffered mass killings of at least 64 people. In Mali, Russian forces have suffered heavy losses, with reports of more than 300 Russian soldiers dead as Moscow supports the military junta. A Russian envoy claims Ukrainian officers are training Sahel armed groups on drones, linking external actors to the insurgency. The Sahel jihadist insurgency caused 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

A 19‑year-old Christian farmer lost a hand in a separate attack, and a land dispute in Niger state sparked dozens of deaths. item.title: Eastern DR Congo: the situation
item.description:
M23 rebels have pulled back from near Bunia after heavy clashes, while fighting intensifies elsewhere as they open a new front near the Uganda border and target Uvira city. WHO evacuated its Ebola response team from a hospital in Ituri after the team was trapped by fighting, and the Ebola death rate is now near 50%. A Congolese military aircraft went missing, with rebels claiming they shot it down, leading to the capture of a South African mercenary and the reported capture of Ugandan and South African nationals. Kenya and the DRC have agreed to restore diplomatic ties after recent tensions. The conflict has displaced 8.2 million people, according to DNE Africa.
